meru-buyback-20b-offered-2b-taken-bill-f:
The US Treasury raised the size of its long-end buybacks from $2 billion to at least $4 billion per operation, and the reason sits in an operation held two days earlier.
In the August 18 operation for bonds maturing in 20 to 30 years, dealers offered roughly $20 billion of paper. The Treasury was permitted to take a tenth of that.

@@REF@@$20 billion offered, $2 billion taken: why Treasury doubled its buyback cap (FXStreet, 2026-08-19)|https://www.fxstreet.com/analysis/20-billion-offered-2-billion-taken-why-treasury-doubled-its-buyback-cap-202608191954

What it actually bought that day was $1 billion of a bond maturing in 2048 and $1 billion spread across two 2051s.
The cap went up at the exact spot where sellers outnumbered the buyer ten to one.

## A buyback is not a repayment

A buyback is the Treasury purchasing back old bonds that are already trading in the market.
The cash for it comes from selling new debt.
Nothing is retired on net. Only the maturity mix moves.

@@FLOW@@Issue bills|Sell new three-month paper to raise cash|Run the operation|Buy old long bonds back from dealers|Shrink the long end|Fewer long bonds circulate, so their price rises and their yield falls@@The path starts and ends at different maturities. Every long bond taken out is replaced by short paper that has to be borrowed again within months.

Long yields do fall along this path.
What remains open is where the cost of that lands.

## Buying 1.9% while issuing at 3.7%

Wolf Street took apart one of the securities bought in this operation.
It is a 30-year bond issued in February 2021, maturing in February 2051, carrying a coupon of 1.9%.
The Treasury bought it at 52.375 cents on the dollar.
That turned $334 million of face value into roughly $175 million of cash paid.

@@REF@@Bessent doubles the buybacks, swapping old cheap debt at a discount for new expensive debt (Wolf Street, 2026-08-19)|https://wolfstreet.com/2026/08/19/bessent-doubles-yellens-hocus-pocus-treasury-buybacks-swapping-old-cheap-debt-at-a-discount-for-new-expensive-debt/

Bought at half price, the face amount of the debt goes down.
But the old bond that disappeared cost $6.3 million a year to service, while the bills issued to fund the purchase cost about $7.0 million a year.
The debt shrank and the annual interest bill grew.

@@CHK@@Three-month bill rate|3.7%|Coupon on the bond bought|1.9%|30-year market yield|5.3%@@The coupon on the retired bond was fixed in the era of cheap money, while the short paper taking its place is priced at today's cost. The gap is narrower than the example in the original post (a 1.4% bond issued in 2020), but it points the same way. What a buyback moves is not the total interest bill but the placement of maturities.@@Retrieved 2026-08-20. FRED DTB3 and DGS30, values as of 2026-08-17. The coupon is CUSIP 912810SU3 as verified by Wolf Street.

The shortening of maturity comes with it.
Three-month paper matures four times a year, and each time it has to be borrowed again at whatever the rate is that day.
While rates sit where they are, that rollover passes quietly. Every rollover is also a repricing.

## What November 4 settles

The increase runs only from the September 9 operation through November 4.
Across seven operations in that window, the extra amount comes to $14 billion.
Against roughly $10 trillion of Treasuries outstanding in the 10-to-30-year sector, that addition is about a tenth of a percent.

So the force of this move is in the sentence rather than the sum.
It told anyone about to dump long bonds in a hurry that somebody is standing there to take them.

If the November 4 quarterly refunding keeps the larger size or raises it again, the interpretation the market bought in August was right.
If the size drops back to the old limit, this becomes a two-month piece of first aid.
What gets settled there is whether the long end is priced by the market or by the Treasury.
How long a price can be held up by changing maturities rather than paying down debt, and what it costs to let that price go, is what is riding on the answer.
serenity-marvell-google-warrant-120b-ves:
Marvell has given Google the right to buy 58.97 million of its shares at $206.58 each.
Exercised in full that is about $12.2 billion of stock, close to 7% of the company.
Marvell rose 12% on the day and traded above $230.

@@REF@@Marvell lands Google AI chip deal, closing the custom silicon hyperscaler sweep (Tech Times, 2026-08-19)|https://www.techtimes.com/articles/324988/20260819/marvell-lands-google-ai-chip-deal-closing-custom-silicon-hyperscaler-sweep.htm|https://d.techtimes.com/en/full/466676/marvell.jpg

A warrant is a right a company issues that lets the holder buy newly issued shares at a set price.
The issuer parts with no cash, and the holder gains as the issuer grows.

## The right does not open by itself

The warrant splits in two.
In year one, 1,360,867 shares vest in equal quarterly instalments no matter what anyone buys.

The remaining 57.6 million shares work differently.
One tranche opens for every $500 million of custom-product revenue Google puts through Marvell, and there are 240 of those tranches.
The clock runs from Marvell's fiscal third quarter of 2027 to the end of fiscal 2033.

@@BAR@@Cumulative Google purchases needed to vest the whole warrant|$120B|1200|Marvell's full-year fiscal 2026 revenue|$8.2B|82@@Google alone would have to buy fifteen times Marvell's entire last-year revenue, cumulatively, for the final tranche to open. The bar on the right is everything the company sells in a year today.@@Marvell fiscal 2026 results (2026-03-05); Tech Times, 2026-08-19

## Is that number a forecast or a condition

@@CMP@@How the market read it|Google has committed to buying that much silicon through 2033, and it lands as Marvell revenue.|What the warrant document says|That figure is the level at which the last tranche vests. Buy less and less vests. It is not a purchase promise.

The same number is a revenue outlook on one side and a strike condition on the other.
Serenity read the deal as something that could translate into revenue of that order through 2033, and how much weight that sentence carries depends on how many tranches actually open.

## Amazon came first

This shape is not new.
Marvell issued Amazon a warrant for 4.18 million shares at $87.77 apiece, tied to purchases of Trainium and Inferentia parts.

With Google, Marvell now holds custom silicon relationships with all three of the big US hyperscalers.
Broadcom, its closest rival in that business, fell close to 3% on the news.

What Google is buying is not the TPU itself but everything that attaches to it.
The agreement covers inference accelerators, storage controllers, network and memory interface controllers, and near-memory compute parts.
The chip supplier hands equity to its customer, and the customer buys more in order to earn it.

## What to watch in the August 27 results

Tranches only start opening in Marvell's fiscal third quarter of 2027.
Once the count of vested tranches appears each quarter, the real size of the Google business becomes visible; if no tranche opens, $120 billion stays an arithmetic figure.
Goldman Sachs has kept a Neutral rating and a $195 price target on Marvell since the announcement.
jukan-samsung-p5-triple-fab-third-floor:
Samsung has filed to redesign the P5 Plant 1 and Plant 2 buildings under construction in Pyeongtaek from the planned two floors to three, according to Korean media reports.
One extra floor takes a single building from four cleanrooms to six, and Samsung reckons capacity would rise by at least half again.

@@REF@@Samsung expands Pyeongtaek fab into triple-deck (BusinessKorea, 2026-08-19)|https://www.businesskorea.co.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=275090|https://www.businesskorea.co.kr/news/thumbnail/202608/275090_282431_1147_v150.jpg

A cleanroom is a space filtered of dust and damped against vibration, and chipmaking tools can only sit inside one.
So when a chipmaker talks about capacity, it is mostly talking about the floor area of these rooms.

## The land stayed the same, the height did not

The Pyeongtaek campus has fixed boundaries, and its power, water and piping are already laid across that ground.
Buying new land means laying all of that again from scratch.

The way to get more rooms on the same site is to stack them.
Samsung asked to raise the floor area ratio ceiling from 350% to 490%.
Floor area ratio is total floor space measured against the size of the lot, so a higher number lets a taller building stand on the same plot.

@@CHK@@Cleanrooms per building, P4|4|P5 as redesigned|6|Floor area ratio ceiling|350% to 490%@@What grew is not the site but the number of decks one building can hold. The same ground yields 50% more cleanroom.@@Retrieved 2026-08-19, from BusinessKorea's account of the Pyeongtaek industrial complex plan revision

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/DDR5_SDRAM_%28with_scale%29_IMGP6298_smial_wp.jpg/960px-DDR5_SDRAM_%28with_scale%29_IMGP6298_smial_wp.jpg|One of the things P5 is meant to turn out: the DRAM sticks that slot into servers.|Smial · FAL 1.3|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:DDR5_SDRAM_(with_scale)_IMGP6298_smial_wp.jpg

P5 is described as carrying high bandwidth memory, high-specification DRAM, next-generation V-NAND and advanced foundry work.
Construction started in 2022 and completion is targeted for 2030, with as many as 50,000 workers on site at peak.

## Why the extra floor, and why now

The earlier lines on the same campus are already full.
Reuters reported that Samsung has raised foundry prices, with Chinese customers absorbing the steepest increases.
Quotes on the 4nm process rose 10-15% for customers in China and the US and 5-10% in Taiwan, while 5nm rose 10-15%.

@@REF@@Samsung raises advanced foundry prices by up to 15% as AI demand fills its 4nm lines (Tom's Hardware, 2026-08-19)|https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/samsung-raises-advanced-foundry-prices-by-up-to-15-percent-as-ai-demand-fills-its-4nm-lines

The number to take from that report is not the percentage but the reason behind it.
Pyeongtaek's 4nm line has reportedly been running full since late last year.
Being able to raise prices means there is not enough to sell now; adding a floor means having more to sell three or four years from now.
In semiconductors that lag between price and plant is always there.

## P5's third floor is still a drawing

The plan has to clear local government approval before it is fixed.
Jukan wrote it as conditional on that approval, and until then this sits on paper.

If approval comes, two things follow.
A three-story P5 means Samsung adds cleanroom on ground it already owns much faster, and the industry expects the fabs planned for Yongin to use the same triple-deck layout.
If the filing is turned down, P5 stays two stories as originally drawn, and the volume plans built on top of it slide back by the same amount.
meru-hanwha-k9mh-mtc-six-prototypes-vs-5:
The US Army on August 18 picked Hanwha Defense USA to build prototypes of a wheeled self-propelled howitzer meant to replace the towed M777.
The award covers six vehicles for $100.3 million, and rises to eighteen vehicles if the Army exercises every option.

@@REF@@South Korea's highly mobile 155mm artillery system wins US Army howitzer contract (The War Zone, 2026-08-18)|https://www.twz.com/land/south-koreas-highly-mobile-155mm-artillery-system-wins-u-s-army-howitzer-contract|https://www.twz.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/army-picks-k9mh-155mm-howitzer-for-prototyping-effort.jpg?w=1200

American Rheinmetall, BAE Systems, General Dynamics Land Systems and Elbit Systems USA competed for the same work. Only Hanwha moved on to the prototype stage.

## What the units towing M777s are trying to fix

The M777 is a gun that a truck or a helicopter drags into position and sets down before it can fire.
Setting up takes time, and so does packing up and leaving.

On a battlefield covered by drones and counter-battery radar, the minutes a crew spends parked where it just fired are the minutes it is exposed.
Firing and immediately moving is what the Army calls shoot and scoot.
Hanwha says the K9MH takes under 30 seconds to emplace or displace.

The Army had been stretching the range of its existing M109 Paladin under a separate effort, ran into limits at the prototype stage, and shut that program down in 2024. After that it turned toward buying a design that already exists.

## The trade wheels make

Self-propelled artillery splits into tracked vehicles and wheeled ones.
Tracks spread the weight of the hull, so a tracked gun keeps moving through mud and up slopes, and it carries thicker armor.
The cost is weight and speed: moving one a long way usually means putting it on something else.

Wheels are the opposite trade.
A wheeled gun is lighter and faster, can drive hundreds of kilometers on its own, and fits inside a transport aircraft.
It pays for that with soft ground and thinner armor.

So the Army intends to leave tracked Paladins with its armored formations and give wheeled guns to the Stryker and infantry brigades that already move on wheels.
Hanwha's entry puts the automated turret of the in-service K9 onto an 8x8 wheeled chassis.

Nothing in the last two has been decided.

## Where the 30 trillion won number comes from

@@CHK@@Signed award (6 prototypes)|$100.3M|Ceiling incl. 12 options|$262.9M|Industry estimate, 500 units|$7.14B@@Two steps sit between the money that has been signed and the 30 trillion won figure circulating in Korean coverage. The $7.14 billion counts the vehicles alone; the larger figure adds ammunition and sustainment on top.@@Retrieved 2026-08-19, from Korea Herald and The War Zone reporting on the Army award, plus industry estimates

@@REF@@Hanwha breaks into US Army market with K9 prototypes (The Korea Herald, 2026-08-19)|https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10845559|https://wimg.heraldcorp.com/news/cms/2026/08/19/news-p.v1.20260819.36f316a3c17c450787190cdfd8474595_T1.jpg

Meru makes the same point about the Korean figure: it counts 500 deliveries plus ammunition and follow-on support on top of them.

## The gate Hanwha has to clear before 2030

What this contract hands Hanwha is not revenue but a position.
Coverage of the award notes that no Korean company had put a complete weapon system into US Army hands before.

The thing to watch over the next four years is the option.
If the Army calls the twelve additional vehicles, it still wants this gun; if the count stops at six, the vehicle was filtered out on the test range.
Read as a contract, this is a low-hundreds-of-millions program. Read as a door, it is the first one a Korean defense maker has opened into US Army procurement.
semianalysis-cerebras-cs4-same-wafer-dou:
Cerebras unveiled CS-4 on August 19, and there is no new chip in it.
The doubling comes from keeping the same 5nm wafer-scale engine, WSE-3, and pushing far more power into it to double the clock.
A rack now holds three wafers instead of two, and a single rack draws 125 to 135 kilowatts.

@@REF@@Cerebras intros faster WSE-3 Turbo processor and first rack-scale CS-4 system (ServeTheHome, 2026-08-19)|https://www.servethehome.com/cerebras-intros-faster-wse-3-turbo-processor-and-first-rack-scale-cs-4-system/|https://www.servethehome.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Cerebras-CS-4-Rack-Hero-Image-scaled.jpg

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/NVIDIA_GPU.jpg/960px-NVIDIA_GPU.jpg|A normal AI accelerator is a single chip about this size. Cerebras never cuts the chip out of the wafer; the whole wafer is the chip.|Mickael Courtiade · CC BY 2.0|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:NVIDIA_GPU.jpg

A chipmaker usually cuts hundreds of rectangular dies out of one round 300mm wafer.
Cerebras does not cut. One wafer is one chip.

## Between 1,950x and 30x

@@BAR@@Cerebras on-chip bandwidth, one wafer|43,000TB/s|43000|NVIDIA Rubin HBM4 bandwidth, one GPU|22TB/s|22@@This is the number Cerebras leads with. Yet the speed advantage the same company claims is up to 30x against GPUs. When two multiples diverge this far, it means bandwidth is not what sets the speed.@@Checked 2026-08-19 · Cerebras CS-4 announcement materials (released 2026-08-18) · NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 product page, 22TB/s of HBM4 per GPU

ServeTheHome quotes 129.6 petabytes per second for a full rack, which is 43 multiplied by three wafers. The two figures agree.

## The 44-gigabyte ceiling

The memory etched into the wafer is SRAM.
It is far faster than the HBM stacked next to a conventional chip, and it holds far less.
One WSE-3 carries 44 gigabytes of it, and that number did not move from CS-3 to CS-4.
The number of storage cells is written into the silicon, so raising the clock does not add any.

Frontier model weights today run from hundreds of gigabytes into terabytes.
They do not fit in 44 gigabytes, so the model is sliced by layer and spread across several wafers.

@@FLOW@@Request arrives|The first wafer takes the front layers of the model|Direct wafer link|Intermediate results cross to the next wafer in 2 microseconds|Final wafer|Finishes the remaining layers and emits the token@@Slicing by layer means every added wafer adds another leg to the journey. What caps tokens per second per user is not bandwidth but the number of those legs and the time each one costs.

Cerebras raised off-wafer I/O bandwidth this generation from 1.2Tb/s to 2.4Tb/s.
Latency through the switched network fell from 5 microseconds to 3, and direct wafer-to-wafer paths get it to 2.
SemiAnalysis still treats that 3 microseconds as a bottleneck.
Spreading expert layers across multiple wafers stays impractical at that latency, which leaves slicing by layer as the only workable option.

## The bill came due in watts

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Datacenter_Server_Racks_%2822370909788%29.jpg/960px-Datacenter_Server_Racks_%2822370909788%29.jpg|One rack draws 125 to 135 kilowatts, the same band as the vendor-published rating for an NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 rack.|Carl Lender · CC BY 2.0|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Datacenter_Server_Racks_(22370909788).jpg

Power per wafer went from 23 kilowatts on CS-3 to roughly 42.
SemiAnalysis therefore reads performance per watt as at best slightly better than CS-3.
What offsets it is the bill of materials: fewer components and simpler assembly should land cost per wafer near where it was.
The pitch to customers is not efficiency but double the token revenue for the same hardware spend.

@@CHK@@Q2 2026 revenue (GAAP)|$180.1m|Cloud revenue, year on year|+281%|Contracted datacenter capacity|600MW@@This company sells chips and also sells inference run on its own chips. Cloud revenue nearly quadrupled in a year, and it has contracted 600 megawatts of datacenter capacity for delivery through the end of 2027. Put the 125 kilowatts per rack against that number and the reason for booking that much capacity in advance becomes visible.@@Checked 2026-08-19 · Cerebras Q2 2026 results announcement (2026-08-12)

@@REF@@Cerebras overclocks WSE-3 waferscale engine to boost inference oomph in CS-4 (The Next Platform, 2026-08-19)|https://www.nextplatform.com/compute/2026/08/19/cerebras-overclocks-wse-3-waferscale-engine-to-boost-inference-oomph-in-nexus-cs-4/5289400|https://image.nextplatform.com/5289403.jpg?imageId=5289403&x=0&y=0&cropw=100&croph=100&panox=0&panoy=0&panow=100&panoh=100&width=1200&height=683

The Next Platform puts the clock at roughly 2.8GHz against 1.4GHz before, with the 900,000 cores and the 44 gigabytes of SRAM unchanged.
It says power and bandwidth figures are being held for a follow-up piece.

## The number Hot Chips settles

Cerebras says fuller detail comes at Hot Chips, which opens August 23.
The figure to watch there is not bandwidth but tokens per second per user.
SemiAnalysis expects CS-4 to land near 4,000 on frontier models, against 2,000 for CS-3.
Reach 4,000 and the company crossed a generation without new silicon; stall near 3,000 and we have seen the limit of what a clock can buy.
elerian-treasury-buyback-double-ycc:
The US Treasury said on August 19 that it will double the size of its long-end debt buybacks, from $2 billion to at least $4 billion per operation.
The increase covers the 10-to-20-year and 20-to-30-year nominal sectors and runs from the September 9 operation through November 4.
On the news the 30-year yield fell 7.8 basis points to 5.2% and the 10-year fell 4.9 basis points to 4.7%.

@@REF@@US Treasury doubles buybacks for long-dated bonds, yields fall (Reuters, 2026-08-19)|https://www.globalbankingandfinance.com/instant-view-us-treasury-double-bond-buy-backs/|https://www.globalbankingandfinance.com/i/cloud-f3c4dccd-7706-48c1-8259-a8db3d2339fd/width=1200,height=630,quality=80,format=auto,fit=cover/

A buyback is the Treasury purchasing old bonds that are already trading in the market.
The cash for those purchases comes from selling new bonds. The total stock of debt does not change; only its maturity mix does.

## $75.2 billion against $577 billion

@@BAR@@Buybacks scheduled Aug to Nov|$75.2bn|752|Net issuance, prior quarter|$577bn|5770@@A buyback does not shrink what the Treasury is printing. Over a comparable stretch, new borrowing runs more than seven times the amount being repurchased. At that size gap it is hard to argue the buyback itself set the long end.@@Checked 2026-08-19 · US Treasury tentative buyback schedule published 2026-08-05 and the quarterly refunding statement of 2026-05-04 (privately held net marketable borrowing, Jan to Mar 2026)

So the number is not what moved yields.
El-Erian reads the market as buying the policy that could come next, not the operation itself.

## Naming the price before you buy

Yield curve control means a central bank or a government pinning a chosen maturity below a set level.
It fixes the price first and then promises to take whatever volume shows up at that price.

Yields do come down when this works.
What the authorities give up is control over quantity, because the sellers decide how much has to be absorbed to hold the line.
Fixing the price means handing over the volume, which is why leaving is far harder than entering.

@@TIME@@1942|The Fed caps long-term Treasury yields at 2.5% and begins buying|1951|The Treasury-Fed Accord ends the cap|September 2016|The Bank of Japan pins the 10-year JGB near 0% under YCC|March 19, 2024|The BOJ ends YCC and negative rates together|>September 9, 2026|First operation at the enlarged size@@It took the United States nine years to walk this back and Japan eight. The door in is wide and the door out is narrow.@@Chicago Fed, "Yield Curve Control in the United States, 1942 to 1951" (2021) · Bank of Japan policy statement, 2024-03-19

@@REF@@Treasury just doubled its bond buybacks: what that can and cannot fix (Benzinga, 2026-08-19)|https://www.benzinga.com/markets/economic-data/26/08/61299914/treasury-doubles-long-term-bond-buybacks

Benzinga's read is that the move eases trading conditions in stale long bonds but leaves the deficit untouched.
El-Erian's caveat sits in the same place.
YCC is not a free lunch, it invites collateral damage and unintended consequences, and the effects of this kind of financial engineering are short dated unless fundamental policy adjustments follow.

## What November 4 settles

The enlarged size only runs to the November 4 quarterly refunding.
If the Treasury raises it again that day, or widens the maturity buckets, the interpretation the market bought on August 19 was right.
If it reverses or simply holds, this week's decline stays a one-day supply reaction.
That is where we learn whether an operation of this size can set the price of a long-bond market worth trillions, or whether the signal that someone intends to set it is enough on its own.
hanke-russia-refining-half-claim-denomin:
What has stopped in Russia is not the wells that lift crude but the plants that turn crude into fuel. Bloomberg's tally of Russian refinery runs fell to 3.6 million barrels a day in July 2026, the lowest since May 2002. Ukrainian drones now reach refineries more than a thousand kilometres from the border.

@@REF@@Russian oil refining falls to 24-year low after Ukrainian drone strikes (The Moscow Times, 2026-08-03)|https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/08/03/russian-oil-refining-falls-to-24-year-low-after-ukrainian-drone-strikes-bloomberg-a93404|https://static.themoscowtimes.com/image/og/ff/93404__ff3faa8a3a1cbf69dd7995191750a478.jpg

## The denominator decides whether it is half

Steve Hanke wrote that half of Russia's refining capacity has been knocked out. That share depends entirely on what sits in the denominator.

@@CMP@@Hanke's reading|Half the nameplate capacity is down. Repairs run into months and more strikes are coming, so stay long gasoline and diesel.|The throughput reading|Russia normally ran 5.3 to 5.6 million barrels a day. At 3.6 million it has lost roughly a third, which is short of half.

The same damage produces two numbers depending on whether you count against the capacity written on paper or against what the plants actually processed in normal times. Russia's nameplate refining capacity is put at roughly 6.8 million barrels a day. Measure against that and the idled share approaches half; measure against recent operating rates and it lands near a third. Ukraine's general staff claimed in early July that 42.7% had been disabled, which is also a nameplate figure and comes from a party to the war.

@@REF@@Ukraine's drones reach 1,500 km into Russia, setting two major oil and petrochemical sites ablaze (Kyiv Post, 2026-07-14)|https://www.kyivpost.com/post/80209|https://static.kyivpost.com/storage/2026/07/14/fa71b1c30b62c3a1d1a429a8b3bd397d.jpg?w=1200&q=90&f=jpg

## Crude piles up while diesel runs short

A refinery is where crude is boiled and separated into gasoline and diesel. When the plant stops, the crude does not vanish. It leaves the country as crude instead.

Prices therefore split in two directions.

More crude looks for buyers and its price is held down, while less refined fuel is made and its price rises. Put simply, the wheat is still there and the mill has burned; what gets expensive is flour, not wheat. On July 8 the US Gulf Coast diesel crack reached 64.58 dollars a barrel, close to a record, and European refining margins were above 60 dollars a barrel in the same stretch. Brent settled at 92.42 dollars a barrel on August 18.

The repair timeline follows from the same physical fact. What burns is the crude distillation unit or the catalytic cracker, equipment that takes a long time to build, and the spare parts and catalysts for it are hard to buy under Western sanctions.

## The door Russia shut until January 2027

@@TIME@@2026-06-28|Ukraine strikes two Russian refineries in one night|2026-07-14|Salavat petrochemical complex hit, 1,500 km from the border|2026-07-30|Russia extends its gasoline and diesel export ban to end-January 2027|2026-08-03|Bloomberg puts refinery runs at 3.6 million barrels a day, a 24-year low|>2027-01-31|Russian fuel export ban scheduled to end@@The strikes are not one event but six weeks of accumulation, and in the middle of it Russia closed its own export door.@@The Moscow Times, Kyiv Post, retrieved 2026-08-19

An export ban is a government conceding that fuel is short at home. Russian domestic gasoline stood at 77.89 roubles a litre on July 27, up 19% from the start of the year. If refinery runs climb back toward 4.5 million barrels a day, the months-long repair estimate was too pessimistic; if they stay below that, the bid under refined product prices carries into winter. Either way, treating crude and refined fuel as if they move together misreads this particular episode.
jukan-skhynix-40t-cancellation-net-cash-:
SK hynix will buy back 40 trillion won of its own shares and cancel every one of them. The board approved the plan on August 19. Based on the previous day's closing price of 1,662,000 won, that is roughly 24.07 million shares, or about 3.3% of shares outstanding. Buying starts on August 20 and runs for about three months, after which the shares are retired.

@@REF@@SK hynix unleashes W40tr buyback amid AI windfall (The Korea Herald, 2026-08-19)|https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10845792|https://wimg.heraldcorp.com/news/cms/2026/08/19/news-p.v1.20260819.7ff4dceaf0ae4cdd95de88e1cba44180_T1.png

## Buying and retiring are not the same

A buyback is a company purchasing its own stock in the market. Shares bought that way can sit in the corporate treasury, and from there they can be resold later, handed to employees as compensation, or swapped for a stake in another company. A buyback on its own therefore does not shrink the share count.

Cancellation erases those shares from the register.

Retired shares never come back, so the number of shares outstanding falls permanently, and the same profit is divided among fewer of them. That is also why Korean policymakers treat the two steps differently. Lawmakers have been debating an amendment to the Commercial Act that would require repurchased shares to be cancelled within a set period, because treasury stock parked indefinitely can protect a controlling shareholder's voting power instead of enlarging what minority holders own. Hours before a 50% tariff on Canadian cars, alcohol and dairy was due to take effect, President Trump pushed the start date back by three days.
The reason given was a deal. The condition attached was that the documents still have to be finalised.

## The law underneath this tariff had already changed

Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 lets the president impose duties of up to 50% on a country that discriminates against American goods.

Goods already covered by Section 232, plus energy, potash, fish and certain critical minerals, are excluded.

South Bow has been sounding out shippers on reusing 150km of pipe already in the ground in Alberta and building a new leg from Montana into Wyoming, with a decision targeted for 2027.

Goods trade between the United States and Canada came to $719.5 billion in 2025.

The length of the pause says most of what there is to say about the deal.
If the documents come together the tariff disappears; if they do not, it lands as written after August 22.

meru-discount-rate-vs-thin-credit-spread:
The 30-year US Treasury yield has climbed to 5.3%, its highest level since 2007.
On the same day CoreWeave fell 8.3% and Fabrinet fell 10%,
while SK Hynix, SanDisk and Western Digital each dropped more than 5%.

@@REF@@Rising Yields, Oil Interrupt Rally, Hurting Chips (Charles Schwab, 2026-08-18)|https://www.schwab.com/learn/story/stock-market-update-open|https://www.schwab.com/sites/g/files/eyrktu1071/files/329122355_2x1.jpg

None of that means these companies will earn less money this year.
What shrank is the rate used to convert that money into today's value.

## Pushing 10 million won ten years out

The discount rate is the rate at which money you will receive later is marked down to what it is worth now.
Put simply, it is an interest rate turned around and run backwards.

Say you are due 10 million won a year from now.
At a 4% rate you only need to put 9.61 million won on deposit today to end up with 10 million,
so that future money is worth 9.61 million won today.
At 5% you need only 9.52 million won.
The same future sum just lost 90,000 won of present value.

Stretch the wait to ten years and the gap changes shape.
At 4% you need 6.76 million won today; at 5% you need 6.14 million.
The same one percentage point now costs 620,000 won, close to seven times the one-year figure.
Compounding does that: interest earns interest, and ten years of it piles up.

## Where banks and tech part ways

A bank that pays a steady dividend hands you money that behaves like one-year money.
The profits an AI company promises sit several years out.
So the same one percentage point moves the two share prices by very different amounts.

That is the first shock, and it arrives fast.
Nothing about the company's earnings changed. Only the price tag attached to those earnings did.

## When the spread is thin, the Treasury yield passes straight through

The second shock is slower.
Companies borrow at the Treasury yield plus a spread that reflects their own credit risk.
A wide spread absorbs part of a rise in Treasury yields. A thin one lets it through untouched.

That is the author's premise, so we went and looked the numbers up.

@@CHK@@30-year Treasury yield|5.31%|10-year Treasury yield|4.72%|10-year real yield|2.44%|10-year breakeven inflation|2.28%|Investment-grade corporate spread|0.81%|High-yield corporate spread|2.70%@@What moved was the real yield, not breakeven inflation. Money itself got more expensive, and this is not an inflation scare. At 0.81% the investment-grade spread is far too thin to absorb the move in Treasury yields, which supports the author's premise. It is still wider than the 0.53% of October 1997, so it is not a record low.@@2026-08-17 · FRED (DGS30 · DGS10 · DFII10 · T10YIE · BAMLC0A0CM · BAMLH0A0HYM2)

When borrowing costs rise, the businesses hurt first are the ones that spend heavily up front and recover it later through usage fees, which is exactly how a data centre works.
The rent has to rise as much as the funding cost did to break even, and when competition stops that from happening, the difference comes out of profit.

@@REF@@Dow, S&P 500 slip on higher oil prices and Treasury yields (TheStreet, 2026-08-18)|https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-aug-18-2026|https://www.thestreet.com/.image/NDA6MDAwMDAwMDAzMTQ3MTM5/nyse-traders-2.jpg?profile=share16-9

As that report notes, yields were not the only weight on the market that day.
Oil rose too, and the two pushed in the same direction on the arithmetic of data-centre investment.

## What Nvidia can answer on August 26

The rule that higher rates sink tech stocks does not always hold.
Rates were high all through 2026, and tech went to record highs anyway.
A discount rate is only the measuring stick. If earnings grow faster than the stick lengthens, the stick loses.

So the question now is not the direction of yields but the speed of earnings.
Nvidia reports its fiscal 2027 second quarter on August 26, and that number is the speedometer.
Revenue and next-quarter guidance above expectations would be evidence that the sector can carry a heavier stick.
Falling short would undercut the very reason the market has been willing to pay these prices at these yields.

The headline growth rate hides a wide spread between categories.
Integrated circuit output rose 20.7% in July alone, industrial robots 30.2%, and computer, communications and electronics equipment 19.1%.

@@REF@@China's domestic demand stays muted in July as retail sales miss expectations (SCMP, 2026-08-17)|https://www.scmp.com/economy/economic-indicators/article/3364266/chinas-domestic-demand-stays-muted-july-retail-sales-miss-expectations|https://cdn.i-scmp.com/sites/default/files/styles/og_image_scmp_generic/public/d8/images/canvas/2026/08/17/d159dbdd-b734-49d4-a138-b197416e5152_3e9ba78f.jpg?itok=Y6pbLR-G&v=1786950005

The domestic imbalance between strong supply and weak demand, he said, is still acute.

## Where the subsidy used to be

What held retail sales up through last year was the trade-in programme, under which the government pays part of the price when an old appliance or car is replaced with a new one.

@@TIME@@2026-07-24|Trade-in budget cut to 250bn yuan, eligible appliance categories reduced from 12 to 6|2026-07-30|Politburo meeting cites effective incremental policy without new fiscal money|2026-08-07|July exports up 23.9%, trade surplus $112.5bn|2026-08-17|July industrial output 4.5%, retail sales 0.6%|>Mid-September 2026|August data release@@The policy arrived in July as words while the money got smaller. ## What Fu Linghui said on August 17

So when do the two tracks become one.
China set this year's growth target at 4.5% to 5% back in March, the lowest band since it began announcing one, and second-quarter growth was reported at 4.3%, already below the bottom of it.

Even if exports and high-tech manufacturing keep growing at double digits, retail sales stuck below 1% leave the target hanging on a single export axis.
If August retail sales, published in mid-September, come back above 1%, the case that July was one month of typhoons and a subsidy gap gets stronger.
If they stay below 1%, the imbalance Fu described looks structural rather than seasonal.
For anyone holding a stock tied to Chinese consumption, that is the reason to read August retail sales before August exports.

## When a cut and a runoff happen together

The answer the market is waiting for is a rate cut.
But what the policy rate moves directly is the short end.

The price of money you get back in 30 years is set by inflation over those 30 years and by how much paper the government prints in the meantime.
When the Fed shrinks its balance sheet, the long-dated bonds sitting in its vault flow back into the market.
The buyers stay the same while the supply grows, so the price falls, and a falling bond price is the same sentence as a rising yield.

@@CMP@@The common reading|If the Fed cuts, borrowing costs come down across the board, so the 30-year eventually follows.|Meru's reading|A cut lowers short rates while balance-sheet runoff pushes long bonds back onto the market. Do both and only the gap between short and long widens.

Readers split on how far the effect of the same cut travels, and what decides the split is not the size of the cut but the balance sheet.

## The resignation Warsh handed in during 2011

Only one tool pulls long yields down directly: quantitative easing, in which the Fed prints dollars and buys long-dated Treasuries.
The Treasury's own buyback swaps stale long bonds for freshly issued bills, so no new money enters the system.
Quantitative easing brings in money that did not exist and removes the long bonds outright. That single difference separates the two tools.

The problem is who holds that tool now. Kevin Warsh stepped down as a Fed governor in March 2011,
and the move is said to have followed his doubts about the second round of quantitative easing pushed by Ben Bernanke.
In 2014 he called quantitative easing a reverse Robin Hood policy that fed the market.
He was confirmed by the Senate 54 to 45 on May 13, 2026, and took the chair on May 22.

@@REF@@Kevin Warsh comes into the Fed facing a big 'family fight' over cutting interest rates (CNBC, 2026-05-16)|https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/16/kevin-warsh-comes-into-the-fed-facing-a-big-family-fight-over-cutting-interest-rates.html|https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/108294756-1776789118294-gettyimages-2271834529-AFP_A8JK6JB.jpeg?v=1776789819&w=1920&h=1080

The piece reports that even before taking office Warsh sat on the side of cutting rates while continuing to shrink the balance sheet, and that the combination was contested inside the Fed.
This is the fuse Meru points at.
The cut is what Trump wants and the runoff is what Warsh wants, and doing both at once can send the 30-year the other way.

## The Senate vote scheduled for September

If the Fed will not move, where is the hand that can hold long yields down.
The remaining route is to issue fewer long bonds, and that requires someone to buy bills instead.

The CLARITY Act, waiting for another Senate vote in September, stands in that spot.
If the bill that sets the rules for crypto markets passes, the regulatory fog over dollar-pegged stablecoins lifts,
and issuers hold most of their reserves in short-term US Treasuries.
Fed Governor Stephen Miran said in a November 2025 speech that the interquartile range of private estimates compiled by Fed staff puts stablecoin uptake at $1 trillion to $3 trillion by the end of the decade.

If that much demand for bills appears, the Treasury can issue more short and less long, holding long yields down by going around them.
If the Senate reaches 60 votes in September, one more hand joins the effort, and if it falls short again what is left is the slow road of waiting for inflation to come down on its own.
So to read the direction of the 30-year now, watching the Fed chair's convictions and the Senate's vote count works faster than watching what else the Treasury secretary pulls out.

## The colors an optical fiber likes

At each end of the cable running between data center racks sits a part about the size of a finger.
Inside that part, called an optical transceiver, an electrical signal becomes light.
The laser that actually produces that light is grown on a base of indium phosphide.

Optical fiber does not carry every color of light equally well.
At 1310 nanometers the signal does not spread, and at 1550 nanometers the least of it leaks away.
Long-distance optical links therefore use only these two wavelengths.

This is why silicon cannot take over the job.
Silicon converts electricity into light so inefficiently that it never becomes a laser, and gallium arsenide does emit light but in the 850 to 980 nanometer range, which is not a color the fiber likes.
Put simply, indium phosphide is close to the only material that can produce the colors the fiber will carry.

It is also why the spread of silicon photonics increases demand for indium phosphide rather than reducing it.
The path the light travels can be etched in silicon, but the place where the light is made still needs a separate indium phosphide chip attached.

AXT, second by share, runs its plant in Beijing.

## Capacitors come in grades

An MLCC is a fingernail-sized part built from stacked ceramic layers.
It holds a little charge and releases it, smoothing the power that runs through a circuit.

MLCCs are graded by how little their capacitance drifts as temperature swings.
X5R drifts more but is cheap and made in volume, which is why it fills phones and laptops.
X6S and X7R hold steadier across a wider temperature range, are harder to build, and go onto AI server boards.

That is the crux.

The two grades mostly come off the same lines rather than separate plants.
Every hour spent printing the upper grade is an hour not spent on the lower one.
